subject: Traffic snapshot & success criteria for trial — next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Traffic snapshot & success criteria for trial — next steps

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a focused 3-week trial that validates cost and latency under your primary workload.

What we captured on the call (high level):
- Primary use case: product search + personalized ranking (API calls on checkout flow).
- Current traffic: mostly US customers, peak during 18:00–22:00 local with nightly batch recompute.
- Key success criteria you called out: 95th pct latency under 250ms for interactive flows, <2% quality regression on top-k recommendations, and cost below your internal threshold (~$0.003 per request equivalent).

To move forward we need a short traffic intake (see bullets below). If you can confirm or provide the CSV, we’ll build a synthetic replay and a short smoke harness.

Workload / traffic details we need (minimal acceptable sample):
- RPS: typical steady-state and 95th-peak (requests per second).
- Token lengths: average and 95th percentile for both prompts and model responses (tokens).
- Concurrency: expected number of simultaneous user sessions during peak window.
- Burst patterns: duration and frequency of bursts (e.g., 10s spikes every 5 minutes, or sustained 15m peaks).
- Payload ratio: percent of requests that include long context (e.g., past 4 msgs) vs short prompts.
- Success metrics: what we should measure for quality (top-k recall, click-through, manual evals).

Proposed trial plan (3 weeks):
1) Week 0 (this week): exchange traffic sample + access plan. Redwood spins up an isolated trial endpoint and a recording/replay harness.
2) Week 1: run synthetic replay at expected RPS/concurrency; baseline latency/cost numbers.
3) Week 2: run live-ish mixed traffic (replay + 10% live) for quality checks; run A/B quality evals.
4) Week 3: finalize report and recommend config (batching/quantization + routing) and handoff for Dedicated sizing.

Owners:
- Brightcart: Samir (traffic sample, approval of success criteria).
- Redwood: Sean (trial lead), Marissa (ops & replay), Karthik (model/config tuning).

Attachments: trial_playbook_v1.pdf — short playbook describing what Redwood needs and the artifacts we’ll produce.

Can you confirm the items above and attach a ~48hr sample CSV (or a small anonymized snippet) we can use to generate the replay? If you prefer, we can take a 2hr live window and replay that — whatever is easiest for your team.

Best,

Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Samir Patel <samir@brightcart.com>

Cc: Brightcart Platform <platform@brightcart.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Traffic snapshot & success criteria for trial — next steps

Thanks Sean — this looks good. Appreciate the clear plan. Quick answers / first pass traffic snapshot below; we’ll attach a sanitized CSV by end of day.

Immediate numbers (estimates):
- Typical steady-state RPS: 12 rps across search endpoints
- 95th-peak short bursts: 120 rps (spikes lasting ~30–90s, mostly between 01:00–03:00 UTC due to EU traffic)
- Concurrency: ~60 concurrent sessions during peak windows
- Token lengths: prompts avg 160 tokens (95p 540), responses avg 220 tokens (95p 980)
- Payload split: ~25% long-context (past 6 messages), 75% short prompts
- Nightly batch recompute creates a 20–30 minute sustained load hitting recommendation endpoint (~200 rps) at 04:30 UTC twice per week

Success metrics: we prefer the latency and quality numbers you listed. For quality we’ll provide an existing holdout to compare top-k recall and a small human-eval set for edge cases.

Attachments: I’ll upload brightcart_traffic_sample.csv (sanitized) shortly. Two quick clarifying Qs:
1) For the synthetic replay, do you need full request payloads or just token lengths + timestamps?
2) Can the trial endpoint enforce a rate cap so we don’t accidentally exceed internal thresholds?

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering | Brightcart
samir@brightcart.com | +1 (646) 222-3344

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightcart.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Traffic snapshot & success criteria for trial — next steps

Hi Samir —

Great, and thanks for the fast turnaround. To answer your questions and make the intake minimal friction: 
- For replay we only need timestamps, endpoint identifier (search vs ranking), token counts (prompt/response), and a small request-type tag. No PII or full user payload required. The CSV schema we prefer is included in trial_playbook_v1.pdf.
- We will provision the trial endpoint with a soft rate cap by default (can be set to your target steady-state + 10%); we’ll coordinate with you on the exact number before running heavy replays.

Proposed short evaluation mapping (what we’ll report):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for interactive search endpoints (ms).
- Cost: per-req tokenized cost and projected monthly burn at your volumes.
- Quality: top-k recall on your holdout, plus human-eval pass/fail on the human set.
- Reliability: request error rate, retry behavior, and KV cache hit rate (if enabled).

Action items (ownership):
- Brightcart (Samir): upload sanitized CSV to the Drive link and confirm preferred rate cap by Mon 11/23 EOD.
- Redwood (Marissa): build replay harness and share runbook + synthetic harness by Tue 11/24.
- Redwood (Karthik): prepare a pre-configured model variant and quantization profile candidate for testing.

If that schedule looks good I’ll lock time for a short onboarding call Monday at 09:00 PT to walk through the CSV schema and runbook.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
